digest.component_or_area: test infrastructure, conftest guards and e2e diagnostics
propositions: A detached pytest run reports errors that do not reproduce in foreground, but the cause is concurrent external mutation of the shared checkout, not detachment itself; detachment merely enables such an actor to exist.

The _no_repo_root_leaks guard in tests/conftest.py misattributes external top-level file writes to the test that happened to run during the write, and deletes those files, silently destroying concurrent agent work.

The e2e browser probe diagnostic in tests/e2e/conftest.py fails to inspect proc.returncode and reports no cause when the child is signal-killed, making a reaped detached suite indistinguishable from a real product regression.

Detached test suites are trustworthy when run in a dedicated worktree with no concurrent mutations; the remedy is documented guidance and honest guard diagnostics that name external-actor possibilities, not a detachment-keyed skip.

The _no_repo_root_leaks guard message must be updated to acknowledge external concurrent processes as a possibility alongside test leaks, and the e2e returncode diagnostic must include the signal or exit code to distinguish reaped children from real failures.
